Author: G.K.Ilanthiraiyan Bench: G.K.Ilanthiraiyan  2024:MHC:4177  BEFORE THE MADURAI BENCH OF MADRAS HIGH COURT  DATED: 17.12.2024  CORAM  THE HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE G.K.ILANTHIRAIYAN  W.P(MD)No.30389 of 2024  and  W.M.P(MD)No.25559 of 2024  Selvi ... Petitioner  Vs  1.The Commissioner,

https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  1/7  For Petitioner : Mr.P.T.Ramesh Raja  For RR 1 and 2 : Mr.D.Gandhiraj  Spl. Government Pleader  For Respondent-3: M/s.M.Aasha  Govt . Advocate(Crl . Side) 
 ORDER This Writ Petition has been filed challenging the order passed by the second rspondent dated 24.7.2024 thereby sealed the premises of the Petitioner 2.3.4 of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2006. 
2.Mr.D.Gandhiraj, learned Special Government Pleader takes notice for the respondents 1 and 2 and Mrs.M.Aasha, learned Government Advocate(Crl.side) takes notice for the third respondent. By consent of both parties, the Writ Petition is taken up for final disposal at the admission stage itself. 
3.The Petitioner is running a shop in the name of Ganesh Store situated at No.186, Kamatchi Nagar,
Vaigai Vadakarai,Ththaneri, Madurai District. The second respondent had inspected the Petitioners shop and found banned tobacco products from the Petitioners shop and ordered to seal the shop itself by https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis order dated 27\4.7.2024.The learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the second respondent has no power or authority to seal the premises under Section 34 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, if the designated officer is satisfied that the health risk condition exists with respect to any food business, he may aftera notice served on the food business operator apply to the Commissioner of Food Safety for imposing the prohibition. In the case on hand, the second respondent. In support of his contention,the learned counsel for the Petitioner relied on an order made in W.P(MD)No.25556 of 2022, ated 5.1.2023 in the case of Kamalakannan .vs. The Commissioner,Tamil nadu Food Safety and Drug Administration Department, DMS Campus, 5th Floor, No.359, Anna Salai, Teynampet, Chennai-6 and others in which it is held as follows:
 6.It can be seen there from t  Designated Officer can only serve em prohibition notice on the food business operaor and then apply to the Commissioner of Food Safety,
who alone can pass an order for sealing the premises. In this case, the Commissioner has passed such an order on 19.10.2022, but the premises came to be sealed on 17.10.2022 itself. This was clearly illegal. The Designated Officer does not have the jurisdiction to seal the premises on his own. 
H o w e v e r , t h e l e a r n e d c o u n s e l f o r t h e P e t i t i o n e r , o n i n s t r u c t i o n s , s t a t e s t h a t https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis he will not claim any damages on this account. This undertaking given by the Petitioner that he will treat the issue as closed, is placed on record.

2 4.Per contra, the learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents 1 and 2 submitted that Rule 2..1.3(4)(1) of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011 permits the second respodnent to seal the premises on certain situations It is relevant to extract the same which reads as under:
2.1.3:Food Safety Officer:
4.Powers and duties(i) Without prejudice to the powers conferred on him under Section 38 of the Act, where the Food Safety Officer is of the opinion or he has reason(s) to be recorded in writing, that in the given situation, it is not possible to omply with the provision of Section 38(1)(c) or the proviso to section 38(1) for reasons like non availability of the food Business Operator, the Food safety Officer may seize the adulterant or food which is unsafe or substandard or misbranded or containing extraneous matter, may seal the premises for investigation after taking a sample o such adulterant or food for analysis.
5.Thus it is clear thateven the Food Safety Officer belong to the rank of second respondent or may seize the adulterant food which is unsafe or substandard or mis-branded or containing https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis extranesous matter,
may seal the premises for investigation after taking a sample of such adulterant or food for analysis. Therefore the second respondent has the power and jurisdiction to sel the premises. That apart, as against the Petitioner, already seven cases registered and out of 7 cases, he found guilty on 3 cases .The case registered against the Petitioner is as follows:
6.The second respondent is under progress to prosecute the Petitioner in the manner known to law. Therefore, the second respondent has rightly sealed the premisses of the Petitioner and thus this court finds no infirmity or illegality in the order of the second respondent. There is no merit in the Writ Petition and liable to be dismissed. 
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 7.Accordingly, the Writ Petition is dismissed. However, the second respondent is directed to complete the enquiry process and pass orders within a period of 12 weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order. No costs. Consequently connected Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
